'''''El grito de Celina''''' ('''''Celina's Cry''''') is a [[List of Argentine films of 1983|1983]] [[Argentina|Argentine]] [[romantic drama film]] directed by [[Mario David (director)|Mario David]], who also wrote the script, which is based on a short story by [[Bernardo Kordon]]. It stars  [[María Rosa Gallo]], [[Selva Alemán]], [[Miguel Ángel Solá]] and [[María Vaner]]. [[Víctor Proncet]] composed the soundtrack.<ref name="Cinenacional">{{cite web|url=https://cinenacional.com/pelicula/el-grito-de-celina/ficha|title=El grito de Celina|publisher=[[Cinenacional.com]]|language=Spanish|access-date=7 July 2020}}</ref> 
The film was shot in 1975, but it didn't premiere until May 1983 due to military government disapproval and censorship at the time.

==Plot==
A mother confronts the young woman who is going to marry her youngest son.

==Production==
The film was produced by executive producer [[Eduardo Thau]].<ref name="Cinenacional"/> The screenplay was written by the director Mario David, based on the short story ''Los ojos de Celina'' by [[Bernardo Kordon]].<ref>{{cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=vOAuAAAAYAAJ&q=David+La+cruz+invertida+1985+Marcos+Aguini|author= Manetti, Ricardo |title=Cine argentino: modernidad y vanguardias, 1957/1983, Volume 2|publisher=Fondo Nacional de las Artes|year=2005|page=402|isbn= 9789500515283 |language=Spanish}}</ref><ref>{{cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=UJFdAAAAMAAJ&q=el+grito+de+celina+1983|title=Efemérides literarias argentinas|author=Paz, Carlos|publisher=Ediciones Caligraf|year= 1999|page=228|isbn=9789879728017|language=Spanish}}</ref> Cinematographer [[Adelqui Camusso]] was hired to shoot the film. [[Víctor Proncet]] composed the soundtrack, while the editing was done by [[Oscar Pariso]].<ref name="Cinenacional"/>

==Reception==
The film was shot in 1975 but because the content and actors were not to the liking of the military government at the time,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://play.cine.ar/INCAA/produccion/376|title=El grito de Celina|publisher=Play.cine.ar|access-date=7 July 2020|language=Spanish}}</ref> the film was censored and blocked from release.<ref>{{cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=QwQaAAAAYAAJ&q=el+grito+de+celina+1983|title=La cultura nacional: examen crítico|author=Eduardo S. Calamaro
|publisher=Librería Hachette|date= 1 Jan 1985|page=261|isbn=9789505061013|language=Spanish}}</ref> It didn't reach cinemas in [[Buenos Aires]] until 26 May 1983.<ref name="Cinenacional"/> The film was critically acclaimed upon release, with Daniel López in ''[[La Voz del Interior]]'' labelling it "Kordon and David's remarkable speech on despotism". Hugo Paredero in ''Humor'' described the actors as "very talented, all deserving", surmising that they must have had "inner drama" to be so convincing to the camera. Jorge Miguel Couselo in [[Clarín (Argentine newspaper)|Clarín]] described it as a "compelling movie" and stated that there are "no decorations". In their 2001 book '' Un diccionario de films argentinos (1930-1995)'', Raúl Manrupe and María Alejandra Portela were less favorable, writing: "Rural matriarchy, rustic beings and critical intention against authoritarianism, in a rather static and outdated realization".<ref >{{cite book|last1=Manrupe|first1=Raúl|last2=Portela|first2=María Alejandra|title=Un diccionario de films argentinos (1930-1995) |page=257|year= 2001|publisher=Editorial Corregidor|location=Buenos Aires| isbn = 950-05-0896-6|language=Spanish}}</ref>
